_comment: DimArch Sage — official color palette. Source of truth for every color value in the DimArch OS repositories.
_structure: Three files. THIS one holds `ramp` (hue families, named after materials) and `role`
(meaning mapped onto them); components reference ROLES, never ramp entries directly.
`components.json` closes the loop: which key of which config takes which role.
`sage-dark.css` / `sage-light.css` mirror the same tokens for consumers that read CSS.
That indirection is the point: a token named `link` cannot be quietly 'unified' into sage
without first answering whether links should be indistinguishable from body text.
v1 of this file described VSCode and Obsidian only, while the real system theme lived
in the dimarch repo and had drifted into three parallel sub-palettes. See _history.
_hierarchy: Sage is NOT one of six equal families. It is the brand, and it dominates:
· ~18% of screen area (all chrome and terminal text) vs ~4% for every accent combined
· loudest tier in the palette — sage.bright 12.49:1, nearest accent 9.9:1
· eight tiers where accents have three, because only sage carries a text hierarchy
sage    = STATE of the interface — active, selected, hover, focus, success, all text
accents = CATEGORY of content   — file type, language, git status, kind of signal
An accent may never mark a state; sage may never mark a category. Same spirit as the
semantic rule below. Without it sage decays into 17% of roles and the theme stops
reading as Sage — measured, not hypothetical.
_distinguishability: THE MEASURED RULE. Two colours that mark DIFFERENT ENTITIES and can appear side by
side must differ by CIE76 >= 18 AND CIEDE2000 >= 9. Both, not either: CIE76 is the
blunter of the two about hue, dE00 about lightness, and each alone lets its own class
of collision through.
DOMAIN — where it applies:
· base tiers of different families
· roles inside file.*, git.*, lang.*, panel.*
· ANSI slots within their group (1-6 among themselves, 9-14 among themselves)
OUT OF DOMAIN — where closeness is the point, not a defect:
· hierarchies: text tiers, surfaces, the eight steps of sage depth
· tiers WITHIN one family. They mark kindred categories on purpose — image and video
are both media, archive and audio both packed. Nine file categories do not fit six
families with every pair above threshold; the fine distinction is carried by the
icon, not the hue. Measured: no arrangement of ochre, patina or cinnamon tiers
clears 18 internally while keeping AA contrast.
· deliberate aliases (urgent == clay.base) — identical values, not near-misses
CALIBRATION, from pairs with a known verdict:
worst 'they blend'   — directory vs branch  CIE76  8.2 / dE00  5.1  (owner's verdict)
archive vs audio     CIE76  6.1 / dE00  4.5
best  'distinct'     — sage vs lichen       CIE76 23.8 / dE00 13.1  (accepted in v2)
cinnamon vs clay     CIE76 20.0 / dE00 13.3
The gap is clean and the thresholds sit mid-way on both scales.
Hue degrees are NOT a metric here and were removed from one: they lie in both
directions. sage->patina was 23° apart (above the old 20° minimum) at dE00 8.3, while
cinnamon->ochre is 17° apart at dE00 21.7.
_geometry: AESTHETICS, not measurement — the companion to _distinguishability, deliberately
separate so neither gets rewritten when the other changes.
Warm natural arc 0° → 176°. The 177–333° range is deliberately empty: no azure, no
violet, no synthetic purple. Rejected on a live test — cold hues fight the warm sage
and read as foreign. Everforest (already in use in this setup's Obsidian and VSCode)
is built the same way: its `blue` is teal 172°, its `purple` is pink 331°.
The complement of the brand, 333° ± 10°, is closed: it breaks the analogous scheme.
heather sat at 334°, exactly there, and was removed for it 2026-07-27.
No minimum spacing in degrees — see _distinguishability for why.
_contrast: base and bright tiers clear 4.5:1 (WCAG AA text).
dim tier is for fills, borders, markers and large icons — NOT small text.
clay.dim 3.09 · patina.dim 4.11 · cinnamon.dim 4.00 clear 3:1 for UI; only sage.dim
(4.82) and lichen.dim (4.21) also clear AA text.
In a muted palette an accent works through DEPTH (lower lightness), not brightness:
an accent at sage's own lightness competes with it and reads dusty. Verified live —
and measured: patina used to sit at sage's exact S and L (28.6 / 61) and was

_note: Light-surface variants. NOT an inversion of `ramp` — the hues are identical but
every value is recalculated: at their dark-surface lightness these accents give
~2.7:1 on cream and are unreadable. Same principle as the dark side pointed the
other way, so `bright` here is DEEPER than `base`, not lighter.
Contrast is solved against the darker of the two light grounds (#f3edd8), so every
value clears AA on both. base targets 4.6, bright targets 6.5.
`dim` is intentionally absent: on a light ground the fill/border role is served by
low-alpha tints of base, not by a separate darker tier.
For ghostty's light profile. Mirrors `ansi` slot for slot, on the light ramp.
The mirrored structural slot is 15, not 0: in the dark palette slot 0 is the
background-adjacent value that can never be a readable foreground, and on a light
ground that role falls to bright white instead. Slot 0 becomes the darkest text.
Everything else clears AA — the profile previously had 11 of 13 colour slots below
the threshold (as low as 2.23), and blue duplicated green's hue exactly, the same
defect the dark profile had.
APPLIED in dotfiles/ghostty/.config/ghostty/light.ghostty. This note used to say
'not yet applied' and was wrong: the profile had been written and was in use, but
the file was missing from components.json, so `palette check` never read it. The v3
accent work therefore left the removed heather in slots 5/13 and the pre-recut
patina in 6/14 without a word. Fixed and mapped 2026-07-27 — a config nobody checks
drifts exactly as fast as one nobody wrote.
Named after materials. Five families sit on the arc — cinnamon, ochre, lichen,
sage, patina — and clay sits outside it, serving a convention rather than the
harmony (see its own _role). `sage_deep` is brand ornament, below the text range
entirely: the logo gradient and low tints.
Removed 2026-07-27: `heather` (334°, the brand's complement — see _geometry) and
`stone`, which was a neutral pretending to be a family and moved to neutral.recede.

_role: BRAND. Eight tiers: carries the full text hierarchy plus brand and state.
`shade` added 2026-07-26 during the herdr pilot — that component uses five
steps of sage depth and the ramp only had four below its accent. Solved at
4.59:1 rather than kept at herdr's own #4a8b6e (4.31, under AA).
Deep sage below the text range — brand ornament, not an interface token.
The logo's radial gradient and the low tint behind starship's clock. All sit
on the sage hue (153°); they are brand derivatives, not foreign colours, and
are listed so no value in the system lives outside this file.
Not for text: these are far below any contrast threshold by design.

clay._role: SEMANTIC ONLY — negative states. Never decorative. clay.base IS `urgent`.
_outside_the_arc: Deliberately does not fit the palette. Red for failure is a cross-platform
convention, and a signal that blends into the harmony stops reading as a signal.
That it 'sticks out' is the design, not drift — confirmed by the owner 2026-07-27.
This is only honest as long as clay stays out of decoration: verified the same day
that every one of its 15 uses is semantic (ANSI 1/9, git.deleted, error notices,
urgent, hyprlock fail, rofi danger, cut marker, write permission).
It is not a rare colour — ANSI 1/9 means it is lit by any red terminal output.
clay._tint_note: Fill behind an error message — rofi's error-message background. Was #2c181c at hue 348; brought to 0. clay.base on it gives 5.05, neutral.primary 13.98.
_dim_note: No consumer as of 2026-07-27 — checked with `palette where`. Kept rather than
removed: every family carries three tiers, and clay's fill/border tier is the one
an error surface would reach for the moment rofi's error box or a critical panel
state needs a border. Retiring it would mean re-deriving the same value later.
3.09 on chrome — fills and borders only, never small text.

_role: Media — images, video, the playing indicator. Added 2026-07-27 to take the
roles heather left behind; without it media had no family of its own and would
have shared lichen with executables at dE00 7.8, below threshold.
Hue picked by calculation, not taste: at 26° it collides with ochre (dE00 6.9),
at 22° with ochre.dim, at 19° the worst pair in the whole palette is 13.3 with
clay. Saturation held inside the palette's own range (52-60 against ochre's 55)
— above that the family reads acid rather than muted.

ochre._role: Change, archives, duration, attention without alarm.
_vivid_note: This is the old `semantic.warning`, moved here 2026-07-27 without changing value.
It is 4° from ochre.base in hue — it was always a tier of ochre that happened to
live in the semantic section. At S 95% it stays outside the muted range on purpose,
so a warning still cuts through. `semantic.warning` now points at this entry.

lichen._role: Executables, Node, caffeine. Fills ANSI blue without a cold hue.

patina._role: Links, documents, symlinks, cool weather. The cold limit of the palette.
_recut_note: Recut 2026-07-27, was #4c7673 / #7fb8b4 / #8fccc8. The old base carried sage's
EXACT saturation and lightness (28.6 / 61) and differed only in hue, by 23° —
so symlink was indistinguishable from directory (CIE76 12.2 / dE00 8.3), weather
from VPN, ANSI 6 from ANSI 2. Seven of the palette's thirteen violations were
Hue could not move: 176° is the arc's cold edge. The fix is depth and saturation
instead — base now 20.4 / 16.4 from sage.base, bright 24.7 / 14.9 from sage.bright.
The deeper, more saturated cut was chosen over a milder one so patina reads as its
own colour rather than a tint of the brand.

_recede_note: Was `ramp.stone.base` until 2026-07-27 — a neutral with a sage bias, for text that
must step back without going cold (neutral.muted is hue 240, outright cold).
It lived in `ramp` as a three-tier family, but herdr's own config records that two
of those tiers have 'no visible effect found': only this one paints anything.
As a neutral it is also out of the distinguishability rule's domain, which it never
passed as a family — it stands beside sage by design rather than against it.
Retired with it: stone.dim #7a8f84 and stone.bright #94a89d.
_muted_note: Raised from #75757f (3.99:1 — below AA) 2026-07-26. That value was set by pixel-sampling
Claude Code's comment color; it stays available as `disabled` for non-text use.

_note: Status colors — meaning, not decoration. Never use for brand accents.
`urgent` is deliberately the same value as clay.base: the clay family is itself
semantic (errors, deletions, broken links, critical load) and appears nowhere
decorative, so the signal is not diluted by sharing one hex.
`warning` IS ochre — 4° from ochre.base in hue. It was moved into the ramp as
`ochre.vivid` 2026-07-27 and is referenced from there; the value did not change.
It stays at 95% saturation, outside the palette's muted limit on purpose, so it
can cut through instantly.
Hue unified to 180° on 2026-07-26 (from 190–195°). At 180° G equals B — the point where
the blue cast disappears but green does not yet dominate. Contrast cost is negligible
(12.67 -> 12.49 to sage.bright).
The old `G>=B` rule is retired as a rule: at this lightness and saturation a shift of
two units per channel is not visible, so it forbade differences nobody could see. Hue
on a near-neutral ground is a tie-breaker between equally good values, not a
constraint — pick 180 when there is no reason to pick otherwise.
An earlier green shift was reverted, but that attempt (#181e1a) changed THREE things at
once — hue, +5pp lightness and a third of the saturation. The 'muddy khaki' reading
likely came from the lightness. A pure hue shift had never been tried.
NEEDS A LIVE LOOK before propagating — see ROADMAP step 1.
Alpha levels are NOT unified: they encode surface depth, not drift.

chrome._use: Translucent glass — waybar (top only), rofi, swaync, swayosd, zathura, hyprlock
_panel_bottom_note: The bottom panel is NOT a second Waybar — that role belongs to dimarch-taskbar
(separate repo, Python + GTK4). Waybar runs a single instance from
config-top.jsonc; the `window#waybar.bottom` rules in its stylesheet are dead.
This token stays valid: it is the reference tone for the taskbar to consume.
Left at hue 190 for now — the top panel moved to 180 on 2026-07-26 but the
shift was invisible side by side, so there is no case for propagating it to a
component that hasn't been themed yet. Decide once the taskbar is styled.
chrome._raised_note: Input fields on glass — rofi's bg-input. Distinct from surface.terminal.raised: same lightness by coincidence, different base underneath.
chrome._alpha_note: rofi 0.72 · waybar 0.78 · swayosd 0.85 · swaync noti 0.85 / cc 0.90

terminal._use: Opaque — ghostty and everything rendered inside it (yazi, starship, uosc, swayimg)
terminal._raised_note: Input/status strips inside terminal apps (zathura). Was #172026 — hue 204.
_border_note: Separators and table rules inside terminal apps (yazi panes, status bars).
Was #3a3a4a — hue 240, inside the cold band the palette rejects. Moved to 180
at the same lightness and saturation; contrast to the terminal ground goes
1.56 -> 1.61, so borders stay exactly as visible as before.
Deliberately low: a divider must be seen without competing with text.
terminal._on_accent_note: Dark text drawn ON sage/ochre fills — a foreground role, not a background.

window._use: Hyprland window frames — deliberately neutral, not sage. Borders sit on arbitrary content.

role._note: What components reference. Values are ramp paths, resolved by the generator.

text._recede_note: Muted section labels and timings — steps back without going cold. herdr's overlay0, starship's cmd_duration.

ui._note: STATE of the interface — sage only. An accent must never appear here.

file._note: CATEGORY of content — accents only. Sage marks only the directory (a navigable state).
_tier_note: Nine categories on six families, so three pairs share a family by tier:
image/video on cinnamon, archive/audio on ochre, symlink/document on patina.
Those pairs sit below the distinguishability threshold on purpose — they are
kindred categories and the icon carries the finer distinction. See
_distinguishability: the rule does not reach inside a family.

_branch_note: Was sage.soft until 2026-07-27, one tier away from the directory it stands next
to in the prompt: CIE76 8.2 / dE00 5.1, physically indistinguishable. On bright
it is 21.4 / 14.4 and becomes the lightest thing in the prompt while staying
inside the brand — this is what sage's eight tiers are for.

_note: At rest the bar is entirely sage. Accents appear ONLY on an event.
HOW THE TWO RULES MEET HERE, settled 2026-07-27 — the general rule says an accent
may never mark a state, and a panel module lighting up IS a state, so the split is
by what the colour has to tell apart:
· binary toggles — VPN, caffeine — take SAGE. On or off; there is nothing to
distinguish, the icon already says which module it is.
· modules where the KIND of signal differs — weather cold/hot/dangerous, mic,
media — take an accent, because the colour carries information the icon does not.
· alarms take `semantic`, never a brand or accent value.
Before this, caffeine sat on lichen and marked a pure state with an accent, while
weather sat on sage.soft in the live config and marked a category with the brand —
the same rule broken in both directions at once.

link._note: Light surfaces need depth, not the dark-surface greens. #35a77c gave 2.74:1 on cream.

_note: Terminal protocol requirement, filled from the palette. Slot 4 (blue) resolves to lichen 88°
rather than inventing a second near-identical cyan: previously blue #6ba88c and green
#7fb89e sat on the SAME hue (152° vs 153°), so the terminal nominally had two colors and
effectively one. Lichen restores a 65° separation without introducing a cold hue.
Slot 0 is a structural slot — never a readable foreground.

_history: 2026-07-12 — semantic section extracted from the dimarch repo (warning, urgent).
2026-07-26 — v2. Audit of ~20 component configs found the theme had split into three
parallel sub-palettes and that this file described none of them. Four orphan colors
removed from dimarch (#2f7d68, #d65d5d, #7c8cd8, #c8cad4), surfaces resynced.
Accent families chosen with an external color audit, verified independently:
19/19 contrast figures confirmed to the hundredth. Rejected from that audit:
clay.base and urgent being presented as unrelated (they are one value by design),
and the loss of #6ba88c, which is pinned by an explicit user request in waybar.
Retired values: #c47a7a #d48a8a (-> clay), #a07fb8 #b08fc8 (-> heather),
#7a9cc4 #8aacd4 (-> lichen/patina), #75757f (-> neutral.muted, kept as disabled).
2026-07-27 — v3. The rule was rebuilt first, then the palette fixed against it.
Distinguishability split out of geometry onto two measured metrics and calibrated
on pairs with a known verdict; it found 13 violations, 7 of them one cause.
· heather removed — 334° is the brand's complement and breaks the analogous scheme
· cinnamon added at 19° — media had no family left and would otherwise have shared
lichen with executables below threshold
· patina recut — its base carried sage's exact saturation and lightness
· ochre gained `vivid`: the old semantic.warning, same value, correct home
· stone retired into neutral.recede — a neutral that had been posing as a family
· git.branch moved off sage.soft, one tier from the directory it stands beside
Retired values: #b87a95 #cd98af #93536e (heather), #7a8f84 #94a89d (stone),
#4c7673 #7fb8b4 #8fccc8 (patina, recut).
